headline: Biological language models are steered by RL and activation control for sequence design
label: Language Models Steering Biomolecular Design
summary: New work couples genomic and protein language models with RL or activation steering for design, while enzyme recommendation tests show mixed evolutionary-feature gains.
synthesis: The dominant thread is controllable generation and selection with pretrained biological language models, steered by external objectives. GENECraft pairs a genomic language model with a functional oracle for regulatory DNA, and ARCADE uses activation engineering to control codon metrics such as CAI, minimum free energy and GC content. CPPainter combines a protein language model ensemble classifier with an RL-guided masked-LM generator, and FusioBERT is a 7.5M-parameter peptide language model for anti-Fusarium ranking. Reinforcement learning also steers structure-based generation toward make-on-demand libraries and optimizes CRISPR spacers under a thermodynamic objective, with strategy-dependent off-target trade-offs. The enzyme item is a cautionary counterpoint: adding MSA Transformer features to EnzymeCage and Horizyn gives mixed gains. New relative to prior benchmark-focused work is the emphasis on steering and objective-constrained generation rather than diagnostic dataset design.
